=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: tests/test_review_surface_prompt_hardening.py
  Line or code reference: _extract_shell_function, lines 42-75
  Problem: The function assumes the opening brace of a shell function appears on a standalone line (stripped == "{"). All shell functions in scripts/review_rb_judge.sh use K&R style where the opening brace is on the same line as the function name — e.g. emit_review_rb_untrusted_file() { at line 177, append_review_rb_semble_query_section() { at line 207, render_review_rb_semble_prefetch() { at line 220. The while loop at lines 44-46 scans past the real function body because lines[brace_line].strip() is never exactly "{", and eventually latches onto the standalone { at line 299 in _resilient_phase_swap(). The extracted block then spans from the target function name through _resilient_phase_swap()'s closing }. The test passes today only by accident: because emit_review_rb_untrusted_file is the first definition in the overshoot range, bash still defines it correctly. If a new standalone { is inserted between the function and line 299, the extraction changes and the test may silently pass with the wrong function body or fail with a parse error.
  Why it fails at runtime: A future edit to scripts/review_rb_judge.sh that inserts an intervening standalone { would change which function body _extract_shell_function returns, causing the test to validate prompt hardening against incorrect or broken shell code instead of the real emit_review_rb_untrusted_file. This is a test-only defect — the production scripts are unaffected — but the test's evidence value degrades to near-zero because the path that matters (the UNTRUSTED_DATA prefixing) was never exercised via the actual shell implementation.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: tests/test_review_surface_prompt_hardening.py
  Line or code reference: _render_integration_conflict_prompt, lines 214-240
  Problem: The function finds the prompt-rendering block in scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh using two brittle positional anchors: (1) the exact line PROMPT_TPL="${PROMPT_TPL}" \ as the start marker, and (2) a later fi line whose joined context contains _smoke_override_tmp as the end marker. This coupling is fragile — any reordering, insertion, or whitespace change to the smoke-override block in the prepare script could cause the test to extract an incomplete or wrong bash block, producing a false negative or (worse) a silent pass on untested code.
  Why it fails at runtime: A refactor of the smoke-override conditional in review_conflict_prepare.sh (e.g. extracting it into a helper function, changing the variable name, or reordering the if block) would cause next(iterator) to raise StopIteration or to match a different fi, yielding a truncated or misassembled prompt-rendering block. The test would then either crash or render a prompt that does not exercise the actual UNTRUSTED_DATA: transport envelope, giving a false sense of coverage. Test-only — production conflict-prepare behavior is not affected.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
